description: Reference to an IP (Intellectual Property) core incorporated in this netlist, if applicable. Links to licensed third-party or internally developed IP blocks (e.g., PCIe PHY, USB controller, ARM Cortex core) for IP usage tracking and license compliance.
reference: IEEE 2000 (IP Reuse Standard), SEMI IP Standards, ITAR/EAR IP Export Controls

description: Foreign key linking to design.eda_tool. Business justification: Netlist is produced by a specific EDA tool; adding eda_tool_id creates a proper reference and removes tool name/version duplication.

Foreign key linking to process.process_flow. Business justification: Netlists are synthesized targeting a specific process flow that determines available standard cell libraries, metal stack options, and timing corners. Synthesis sign-off reports reference the process

Foreign key linking to product.ic_catalog. Business justification: Netlist release management and ECO tracking require direct traceability from a synthesized netlist to its IC catalog entry. Netlist-level sign-off reports and tapeout readiness dashboards query netlis

Reference to the Process Design Kit (PDK) version used during logic synthesis. The PDK defines the standard cell library, design rules, and technology parameters for the target fabrication process node.
reference: SEMI P10 (PDK Standard), Cadence Virtuoso PDK Framework

description: Reference to the RTL specification artifact from which this netlist was synthesized. Establishes design provenance traceability from RTL source to synthesized gate-level netlist.
reference: IEEE 1364 (Verilog HDL Standard), IEEE 1800 (SystemVerilog Standard), Siemens Teamcenter PLM

description: FK to design.ic_design_project.ic_design_project_id — Netlist belongs to a design project. Required for project-level artifact tracking and version management.
FK to design.pdk.pdk_id — Synthesis uses PDK standard cell libraries. The netlist must reference which PDK version was used for synthesis.

FK to design.rtl_specification.rtl_specification_id — A netlist is synthesized from an RTL specification. This is the core design flow linkage (RTL -> synthesis -> netlist) required for design provenance.
Date and time when the netlist was formally approved for promotion to the next design stage. Supports design review audit trails and milestone tracking for tapeout schedule management.
reference: Siemens Teamcenter PLM Approval Workflow, ISO 9001 (Quality Management Systems)

description: Estimated silicon area of the synthesized netlist in square micrometers (µm²) as reported by the synthesis tool. Represents the combinational and sequential cell area before physical placement. A key PPA (Power-Performance-Area) metric.
reference: Synopsys Design Compiler Area Report, SEMI Standards

description: Total number of standard cell instances instantiated in the synthesized netlist. Distinct from gate count — counts actual cell placements including sequential elements (flip-flops, latches) and combinational cells.
reference: Synopsys Design Compiler Cell Count Report

description: Name of the standard cell library used during logic synthesis (e.g., 'TSMC_N5_SC_HD_v1.2'). Defines the set of logic gates, flip-flops, and combinational cells mapped during synthesis from the PDK.
reference: SEMI P10 (PDK Standard), Synopsys Design Compiler Liberty (.lib) Format

description: Version identifier of the standard cell library used during synthesis. Critical for design reproducibility and provenance — different library versions may have different timing, power, or area characteristics.
reference: Synopsys Liberty (.lib) Format, SEMI P10 (PDK Standard)

description: SHA-256 cryptographic hash of the netlist file content. Used to verify file integrity, detect unauthorized modifications, and ensure design provenance authenticity across EDA tool handoffs and IP delivery.
reference: NIST FIPS 180-4 (SHA-256), ITAR (Design IP Protection), EAR (Export Administration Regulations)

description: Number of combinational logic cells (AND, OR, MUX, inverters, etc.) in the synthesized netlist. Used for area estimation and logic optimization analysis during PPA (Power-Performance-Area) evaluation.

File path or repository reference to the Synopsys Design Constraints (SDC) file used during synthesis. The SDC file specifies timing constraints, clock definitions, input/output delays, and false paths that govern synthesis optimization.
reference: Synopsys Design Constraints (SDC) Format Standard, IEEE 1801 (UPF)

description: Date and time when this netlist record was first created in the data platform. Supports audit trail, data lineage, and Silver layer ingestion tracking for the design domain.
reference: ISO 9001 (Quality Management Systems), SOX (Sarbanes-Oxley Act - Data Audit Trail)

description: Propagation delay of the longest (critical) timing path in the synthesized netlist, measured in picoseconds (ps). Determines the maximum achievable operating frequency and is a key PPA (Power-Performance-Area) metric for design optimization.
reference: Synopsys PrimeTime Static Timing Analysis (STA), IEEE 1801

description: Name of the IC design block or module represented by this netlist (e.g., 'ALU', 'memory_controller', 'pcie_phy'). Corresponds to the top-level module name in the RTL hierarchy submitted to the synthesis tool.
reference: IEEE 1364 (Verilog HDL), IEEE 1800 (SystemVerilog), Synopsys Design Compiler

description: Sequential iteration counter for synthesis runs on the same design block. Increments with each new synthesis attempt, enabling tracking of design convergence progress and comparison of PPA metrics across iterations.
reference: Siemens Teamcenter PLM Revision Management, Oracle Agile PLM

business_glossary_term: Design for Manufacturability (DFM) Rule Check Status
description: Status of Design for Manufacturability (DFM) rule checks applied to this netlist. DFM rules ensure the synthesized design is compatible with the target fabrication process constraints to maximize yield.
reference: SEMI Standards, Synopsys IC Compiler DFM, ITRS/IRDS Roadmap

business_glossary_term: Design for Testability (DFT) Scan Coverage Percentage
description: Percentage of sequential elements covered by DFT (Design for Testability) scan chains in the synthesized netlist. Higher coverage improves defect detection during Automatic Test Equipment (ATE) testing. Target is typically ≥95% for production designs.
reference: JEDEC JESD22 (DFT Standards), IEEE 1149.1 (JTAG Boundary Scan), Synopsys DFT Compiler

description: Estimated dynamic (switching) power consumption in milliwatts (mW) from the synthesis power analysis report. Represents power consumed by logic transitions and is activity-dependent. Used for thermal and battery life analysis.
reference: Synopsys Design Compiler Power Report, IEEE 1801 (UPF)

description: Repository or file system path to the synthesized netlist artifact file (e.g., '/design/proj/cpu_core/syn/v3/cpu_core_top.v'). Enables EDA tool flows and downstream physical design steps to locate and consume the netlist.
reference: Siemens Teamcenter PLM Document Management, Oracle Agile PLM

description: File format of the synthesized netlist artifact (e.g., Verilog gate-level netlist, VHDL, SPICE, EDIF, Liberty). Determines compatibility with downstream EDA tools for physical design, simulation, and verification flows.

Total number of logic gates (expressed in equivalent 2-input NAND gate equivalents) in the synthesized netlist. A primary measure of design complexity and silicon area consumption used for Power-Performance-Area (PPA) analysis.
reference: Synopsys Design Compiler Area Report, IEEE 1364

description: Estimated static leakage power consumption in microwatts (µW) from the synthesis power analysis report. Represents power consumed when the circuit is idle due to sub-threshold leakage currents. Critical for low-power and IoT product designs.
reference: Synopsys Design Compiler Power Report, IEEE 1801 (UPF)

description: Human-readable name assigned to the netlist artifact, typically reflecting the design block name and synthesis iteration (e.g., 'cpu_core_top_postsyn_v3'). Used for identification in EDA tool flows and design review sessions.
reference: Synopsys Design Compiler Naming Conventions, IEEE 1364

description: Classification of the netlist stage in the IC design flow: pre_synthesis (RTL-level functional netlist before synthesis), post_synthesis (gate-level netlist after logic synthesis by Synopsys Design Compiler), or post_layout (netlist annotated with parasitic extraction data after physical design in Cadence Innovus).
reference: Synopsys Design Compiler User Guide, Cadence Innovus Implementation System, IEEE 1364

description: Number of sequential logic cells (flip-flops, latches, registers) in the synthesized netlist. Used for Design for Testability (DFT) scan chain planning and power analysis of dynamic switching activity.
reference: Synopsys Design Compiler, JEDEC JESD22 (DFT Standards)

description: Date and time when the logic synthesis run that produced this netlist was executed. Provides the principal business event timestamp for design provenance, audit trails, and design iteration tracking.
reference: Synopsys Design Compiler Run Log, Siemens Teamcenter PLM Audit Trail

description: Wall-clock runtime of the synthesis job in minutes. Used for EDA compute resource planning, license utilization tracking, and identifying synthesis runs that exceed expected runtimes due to design complexity or tool issues.
reference: Synopsys Design Compiler Run Log, EDA License Management

description: Current lifecycle status of the netlist artifact within the design flow. Tracks progression from initial synthesis run through completion, failure, archival, or supersession by a newer version.
reference: Siemens Teamcenter PLM Lifecycle States, Oracle Agile PLM

description: Planned tapeout date for the IC design project associated with this netlist. Used to assess synthesis schedule adherence and Time-to-Market (TTM) risk. Tapeout is the final design submission milestone for manufacturing.
reference: Siemens Teamcenter PLM Project Schedule, SEMI Standards

description: Target operating clock frequency in megahertz (MHz) specified in the synthesis constraints (SDC). Defines the timing closure goal for the synthesis run and is used to evaluate whether timing slack objectives are met.

Indicates whether timing closure has been achieved for this netlist (True = all timing paths meet constraints with non-negative slack; False = timing violations remain). A prerequisite gate for advancing to physical design and tapeout.
reference: Synopsys PrimeTime Static Timing Analysis (STA), IEEE 1801

description: Worst-case hold timing slack in picoseconds (ps) across all timing paths in the synthesized netlist, as reported by Synopsys PrimeTime. Negative hold slack indicates a hold violation requiring buffer insertion or path adjustment.
reference: Synopsys PrimeTime Timing Analysis, JEDEC Timing Standards

description: Worst-case setup timing slack in picoseconds (ps) across all timing paths in the synthesized netlist, as reported by Synopsys PrimeTime. Negative slack indicates a timing violation (setup violation) that must be resolved before tapeout. Critical PPA metric.
reference: Synopsys PrimeTime Timing Analysis, IEEE 1801 (UPF), JEDEC Timing Standards

description: Total number of timing path violations (setup and hold combined) reported in the synthesis timing analysis. A value of zero indicates timing closure has been achieved. Used to track synthesis convergence progress across iterations.

Estimated total power consumption of the synthesized netlist in milliwatts (mW), as reported by the synthesis tool. Includes dynamic switching power and static leakage power. A key PPA (Power-Performance-Area) metric for product qualification.
reference: Synopsys Design Compiler Power Analysis, IEEE 1801 (UPF - Unified Power Format)

description: Date and time when this netlist record was last modified in the data platform. Used for incremental data pipeline processing, change detection, and audit trail maintenance in the Databricks Silver layer.
reference: ISO 9001 (Quality Management Systems), SOX (Sarbanes-Oxley Act - Data Audit Trail)

description: Version identifier for the netlist artifact following semantic versioning conventions (e.g., 'v1.0', 'v2.3.1'). Tracks netlist iterations across design synthesis runs to support design provenance and change management.
reference: Oracle Agile PLM Change Management, Siemens Teamcenter PLM

description: Unique surrogate identifier for each physical design layout record in the Databricks Silver Layer. Serves as the primary key for the physical_layout data product.

Foreign key linking to design.eda_tool. Business justification: physical_layout has eda_tool (STRING) and eda_tool_version (STRING) as denormalized EDA tool references — the P&R tool used to produce the layout (e.g., Cadence Innovus, Synopsys ICC2). Adding eda_too
Foreign key linking to equipment.fab_tool. Business justification: Physical layout files are assigned to a specific fab tool for mask generation; required by the 'Layout‑to‑Tool Assignment' process.

Foreign key linking to process.process_flow. Business justification: Physical layout implementation (place-and-route, DRC, CMP fill) is performed against a specific process flow's design rule decks and metal stack definition. DRC sign-off and tapeout readiness reviews

Foreign key linking to product.ic_catalog. Business justification: Physical layout sign-off, DFM scoring, and yield prediction reports are tied directly to the IC catalog entry. Layout engineers query layouts by product in PDM/PLM systems. The indirect path via ic_de
FK to design.netlist.netlist_id — Physical layout (place and route) takes a netlist as input. This is the core PnR flow linkage required for design provenance.

Reference to the Process Design Kit (PDK) version used for this physical layout. The PDK defines the technology node rules, design rule checks (DRC), and layer stack for the target fabrication process.
reference: SEMI P10 (PDK Standard); Foundry PDK Documentation

description: FK to design.ic_design_project.ic_design_project_id — Physical layouts belong to a specific IC design project. Required for design artifact management.
Reference to the parent IC design record for which this physical layout iteration was produced. Links the layout to its originating design project.

Number of antenna rule violations detected in the layout. Antenna violations occur when metal segments accumulate charge during plasma etching that can damage gate oxide. Must be resolved or mitigated with antenna diodes before tapeout.
reference: Foundry Antenna Rule Specification; SEMI P10

description: Percentage of the core area occupied by placed standard cells, expressed as a decimal percentage (e.g., 72.500 = 72.5%). High utilization (>85%) may indicate routing congestion risk; low utilization (<50%) may indicate oversized floorplan.
Area of the core logic region in square millimeters (mm²), excluding I/O ring, power ring, and seal ring. Used to assess logic density and available routing resources.
Timestamp when this physical layout record was first created in the data platform. Used for audit trail and data lineage tracking in the Databricks Silver Layer.
reference: SOX Section 404 (Audit Trail); ISO 9001 Quality Records

description: Clock insertion delay in picoseconds (ps) from the clock source to the farthest clock sink in the clock tree. Impacts setup timing margin and must be accounted for in static timing analysis (STA).
reference: Cadence Innovus CTS Report; Synopsys PrimeTime STA

description: Clock skew in picoseconds (ps) achieved by the Clock Tree Synthesis (CTS) engine at this layout iteration. Measures the maximum difference in clock arrival times across all sink flip-flops. Lower skew improves timing closure margin.

Quantitative DFM (Design for Manufacturability) score assigned to this layout iteration by the DFM analysis tool (e.g., Mentor Calibre YieldAnalyzer). Higher scores indicate better manufacturability and expected yield; used to guide layout optimization before tapeout.
reference: SEMI P10; Mentor Calibre DFM; IEEE 1687

description: Fault coverage percentage achieved by the DFT (Design for Testability) implementation at this layout stage, as reported by ATPG (Automatic Test Pattern Generation) tools. Typically required to exceed 95% for production test qualification.
reference: IEEE 1149.1 (JTAG Boundary Scan); Mentor Tessent ATPG; JEDEC

description: Total die area in square millimeters (mm²) computed from the floorplan boundary. A primary PPA (Power, Performance, Area) metric used for cost estimation, yield modeling, and competitive benchmarking.
Height of the die boundary in micrometers (µm) as defined in the physical layout floorplan. Together with die width, determines die area for yield and cost analysis.
reference: JEDEC JESD30 (Package Outline Standards); SEMI M1

description: Width of the die boundary in micrometers (µm) as defined in the physical layout floorplan. Used for package selection, wafer yield estimation, and cost modeling.
reference: JEDEC JESD30 (Package Outline Standards); SEMI M1

business_glossary_term: Critical Design Rule Check (DRC) Violation Count
description: Number of DRC violations classified as critical (yield-impacting or functionality-blocking) as opposed to waivable violations. Critical DRC violations must be resolved before tapeout; waivable violations may be accepted with foundry approval.
reference: Foundry DRC Runset Specification; SEMI P10

description: Total number of Design Rule Check (DRC) violations detected in this layout iteration by the signoff DRC tool (e.g., Mentor Calibre, Synopsys IC Validator). A value of zero is required for tapeout approval.
reference: SEMI P10 (DRC Rules); Foundry DRC Runset Specification

description: Indicates whether all metal interconnects in the layout comply with electromigration (EM) current density limits specified by the foundry PDK. TRUE = EM compliant; FALSE = EM violations present requiring wire widening or rerouting.
reference: Foundry EM Design Rules; JEDEC JEP122 (Electromigration)

description: SHA-256 cryptographic checksum of the GDSII/OASIS layout file for integrity verification. Used to confirm that the submitted tapeout file has not been corrupted or tampered with during transfer to the foundry.
reference: NIST FIPS 180-4 (SHA-256); Foundry Tapeout Submission Requirements

description: Format of the layout database file referenced in gds_file_path. GDSII is the traditional foundry submission format; OASIS (Open Artwork System Interchange Standard) is the modern compressed alternative; LEF/DEF is used for abstract/physical exchange.

business_glossary_term: Graphic Data System II (GDSII) File Path
description: File system or object storage path to the GDSII (Graphic Data System II) or OASIS layout database file for this physical layout iteration. The GDSII file is the primary deliverable submitted to the foundry for mask generation at tapeout.
reference: SEMI P10 (GDSII Standard); Calma GDSII Stream Format

description: Current stage in the physical implementation flow for this layout iteration. Stages progress from initial floorplan through placement, clock tree synthesis (CTS), routing, signoff, and final tapeout submission. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: floorplan|placement|cts|routing|signoff|tapeout — promote to reference product if additional stages are needed]
reference: Cadence Innovus Physical Implementation Flow; IEEE 1801 (UPF Power Intent)

description: Maximum static IR drop in millivolts (mV) observed in the power grid analysis at this layout iteration. Excessive IR drop degrades circuit performance and reliability; must remain within foundry-specified limits for tapeout approval.
reference: Cadence Voltus Power Integrity Analysis; IEEE 1801 (UPF)

description: Timestamp when this physical layout iteration checkpoint was captured and committed to the design database. Represents the principal business event time for this layout record, enabling chronological tracking of design progress.
reference: Cadence Innovus Design Checkpoint; Siemens Teamcenter PLM

description: Human-readable name identifying this physical layout iteration, typically including the design name and iteration label (e.g., 'SoC_v3_floorplan_iter2'). Used in Cadence Innovus and Synopsys ICC2 project naming conventions.

Lifecycle status of this physical layout record. Tracks whether the layout is actively being worked on, under design review, approved for next stage, rejected requiring rework, or archived as a historical iteration.
reference: Oracle Agile PLM Lifecycle Management; Siemens Teamcenter PLM

description: Version identifier for this physical layout iteration following semantic versioning (e.g., '1.0.0', '2.3.1'). Tracks incremental changes through the physical implementation flow from floorplan to tapeout.

Static leakage power in microwatts (µW) estimated for this layout at the target operating conditions. Critical for battery-powered and low-power IoT/mobile applications; tracked separately from dynamic power for PPA optimization.

Indicates whether the physical layout passes Layout Versus Schematic (LVS) verification with zero errors, confirming that the layout netlist matches the schematic netlist. TRUE = LVS clean (required for tapeout); FALSE = LVS errors present.
reference: Mentor Calibre LVS; Synopsys Hercules; SEMI P10

description: Average metal fill density percentage across all metal layers after dummy metal fill insertion. Foundry CMP (Chemical Mechanical Planarization) processes require metal density to remain within specified min/max bounds to ensure planar surfaces.
reference: Foundry CMP Metal Fill Rules; SEMI P10

description: Number of metal routing layers used in this physical layout, as defined by the PDK technology node stack (e.g., 12 for advanced FinFET nodes). Determines routing resource availability and BEOL (Back End of Line) complexity.
reference: SEMI P10 (PDK Layer Stack); ITRS Roadmap

description: Free-text notes capturing design decisions, known issues, waiver justifications, or iteration-specific observations recorded by the physical design engineer. Supports design review documentation and knowledge transfer.
reference: Oracle Agile PLM Change Management; Siemens Teamcenter PLM

description: Estimated total power consumption in milliwatts (mW) from power analysis at this layout iteration, including dynamic switching power and static leakage power. A key PPA (Power, Performance, Area) metric for product specification compliance.
reference: Cadence Voltus Power Analysis; Synopsys PrimePower; IEEE 1801 (UPF)

description: Metal layer identifier (e.g., 'M4', 'M7') where the maximum routing congestion was observed. Used to guide targeted floorplan or placement adjustments to relieve congestion on the most constrained layer.

Maximum routing congestion percentage observed across all metal layers in the layout, expressed as overflow percentage. Values above 5% typically indicate routing closure risk requiring floorplan or placement adjustment.
reference: Cadence Innovus Routing Congestion Report; IEEE 1481

description: Date on which the final GDSII/OASIS layout was submitted to the foundry for mask generation (tapeout). A critical milestone in the IC design lifecycle tracked against the product TTM (Time to Market) schedule.
reference: Siemens Teamcenter PLM Milestone Tracking; SEMI

description: Total Negative Slack (TNS) in picoseconds (ps), representing the sum of all negative slack values across all timing paths. Indicates the overall magnitude of timing violations in the design; must reach zero for tapeout signoff.

Total number of standard cells placed in the core area at this layout iteration. Includes combinational logic, sequential elements, buffers, and inverters. Used to assess design complexity and placement density.
Timestamp when this physical layout record was last modified in the data platform. Supports incremental data processing, change detection, and audit compliance in the Databricks Silver Layer.
reference: SOX Section 404 (Audit Trail); ISO 9001 Quality Records

description: Worst Negative Slack (WNS) in picoseconds (ps) from static timing analysis at this layout iteration. Negative values indicate timing violations; zero or positive values indicate timing closure. A key metric for tapeout readiness.
Unique surrogate identifier for the RTL specification record in the lakehouse. Primary key for this data product.
reference: Siemens Teamcenter PLM; IEEE Std 1364 (Verilog); IEEE Std 1076 (VHDL)

description: Foreign key linking to design.pdk. Business justification: An RTL specification targets a specific PDK (process design kit) for synthesis and implementation. rtl_specification.pdk_version is a denormalized STRING reference to the PDK. Adding pdk_id as a prope

Reference to the IP license agreement governing the use of third-party or licensed IP content within this RTL specification. Populated when ip_reuse_source is 'licensed_third_party'. Supports IP compliance and NRE cost tracking.
reference: Oracle Agile PLM; ITAR; EAR; IEEE Std 1800

description: Reference to the Multi-Project Wafer (MPW) shuttle run assigned for prototype fabrication of this RTL design. MPW shuttles allow multiple designs to share a single wafer to reduce NRE costs for early silicon validation.
reference: SEMI Standards; Camstar MES; SAP S/4HANA (PP)

description: FK to design.ic_design_project.ic_design_project_id — Every RTL specification belongs to exactly one IC design project. This is the fundamental parent-child relationship for design artifacts. Engineers navigate from project to RTL modules daily.

Reference identifier or path to the Verilog-AMS or VHDL-AMS behavioral model associated with this analog/mixed-signal RTL block. Populated only when is_analog_mixed_signal is True. Links to the Cadence Virtuoso schematic source.

Completion status of Clock Domain Crossing (CDC) boundary annotations within the RTL specification. CDC annotation is mandatory for multi-clock designs prior to synthesis sign-off to prevent metastability failures.
reference: IEEE Std 1800; Synopsys Design Compiler; JEDEC

description: Number of distinct clock domains defined within this RTL design block. Drives Clock Domain Crossing (CDC) analysis requirements and verification complexity estimation.
reference: IEEE Std 1800; Synopsys Design Compiler; Cadence Innovus

description: The specific commit hash or changelist number in the revision control system corresponding to the approved version of this RTL specification. Provides immutable provenance linkage to the exact source snapshot.
Timestamp when this RTL specification record was first created in the system of record. Provides audit trail for design provenance and compliance with ISO 9001 design record retention requirements.

Human-readable name of the RTL design block, IP subsystem, or full-chip entity described by this specification (e.g., 'USB3_PHY_Controller', 'DDR5_Memory_Interface', 'Top_Level_SoC'). Serves as the primary identity label for the design artifact.
reference: IEEE Std 1364; IEEE Std 1800 (SystemVerilog); Cadence Virtuoso

description: Classification of the RTL design block scope. Determines applicable design rules, verification methodology, and integration requirements. 'ip_core' blocks are subject to IP licensing tracking; 'fpga_target' blocks require device-specific synthesis constraints. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: full_chip|subsystem|ip_core|interface_block|analog_mixed_signal|fpga_target — promote to reference product]
reference: IEEE Std 1800; JEDEC; Cadence Virtuoso and Innovus

description: Narrative description of the functional design intent, architectural decisions, and key requirements captured in this RTL specification. Provides context for design reviews, IP reuse assessments, and new engineer onboarding.
reference: Siemens Teamcenter PLM; IEEE Std 1800; ISO 9001

business_glossary_term: Design for Manufacturability (DFM) Rule Set Version
description: Version identifier of the Design for Manufacturability (DFM) rule set applied to this RTL specification. DFM rules ensure the design can be reliably manufactured at the target process node with acceptable yield.
reference: SEMI Standards; Cadence Innovus; Synopsys Design Compiler

description: Design for Testability (DFT) methodology applied to this RTL block. Defines the test insertion approach used to enable Automatic Test Pattern Generation (ATPG) and silicon test coverage on Automatic Test Equipment (ATE).
reference: IEEE Std 1149.1 (JTAG/Boundary Scan); JEDEC; Synopsys Design Compiler

business_glossary_term: Export Administration Regulations (EAR) Export Control Classification Number (ECCN)
description: Export Control Classification Number (ECCN) assigned to this RTL specification under the Export Administration Regulations (EAR). Determines export licensing requirements for cross-border transfer of design data.
reference: BIS/EAR (15 CFR Parts 730-774); ITAR; CHIPS Act Compliance

business_glossary_term: Field-Programmable Gate Array (FPGA) Target Device Family
description: Target FPGA device family for synthesis and implementation (e.g., 'Xilinx Ultrascale+', 'Intel Agilex', 'Lattice ECP5'). Populated only when is_fpga_target is True. Determines device-specific synthesis constraints and IP primitives.
reference: JEDEC; IEEE Std 1364; Synopsys Design Compiler

description: Target functional coverage percentage defined in the verification plan for this RTL specification. Expressed as a percentage (0.00–100.00). Used to gate simulation sign-off and tapeout readiness reviews.

Primary Hardware Description Language used to author the RTL source code for this design block. Determines EDA tool compatibility, lint rule sets, and synthesis flow configuration in Synopsys Design Compiler.
reference: IEEE Std 1364 (Verilog); IEEE Std 1800 (SystemVerilog); IEEE Std 1076 (VHDL); JEDEC

description: Comma-separated list of hardware interface protocols implemented in this RTL block (e.g., 'AXI4, AHB5, APB3, Wishbone, PCIe, USB3'). Used for integration compatibility checks and IP reuse assessments.
reference: AMBA AXI Specification (ARM); IEEE Std 1149.1; JEDEC

description: Origin classification of the IP content in this RTL specification. 'licensed_third_party' requires IP license compliance tracking; 'open_source' requires license obligation management (e.g., GPL, Apache); 'internal' indicates proprietary reuse. Classified confidential due to IP licensing sensitivity.
reference: ITAR; EAR; IEEE Std 1800; Oracle Agile PLM

description: Indicates whether this RTL specification includes analog or mixed-signal content requiring behavioral model references (Verilog-AMS, VHDL-AMS) and linkage to transistor-level schematic source in Cadence Virtuoso.
reference: IEEE Std 1076.1 (VHDL-AMS); Cadence Virtuoso; SEMI Standards

description: Indicates whether this RTL specification is intended for FPGA implementation rather than ASIC tapeout. When True, synthesis constraints, pin assignments, and target device family fields are applicable.
reference: IEEE Std 1364; JEDEC; Synopsys Design Compiler

business_glossary_term: International Traffic in Arms Regulations (ITAR) Controlled Indicator
description: Indicates whether this RTL specification is subject to International Traffic in Arms Regulations (ITAR) export controls. When True, access must be restricted to authorized US persons and export license requirements apply.
reference: ITAR (22 CFR Parts 120-130); BIS/EAR; US Department of State

description: Timestamp of the most recent modification to this RTL specification record. Used for change tracking, incremental data pipeline processing, and audit compliance.

Status of RTL lint rule compliance checks for this specification. Lint tools (e.g., Synopsys SpyGlass, Cadence HAL) enforce coding guidelines and detect potential design errors. 'clean' is required before synthesis sign-off.
reference: Synopsys Design Compiler; IEEE Std 1800; ISO 9001

description: Estimated number of equivalent logic gates for this RTL design block, derived from synthesis estimation runs in Synopsys Design Compiler. Used for area budgeting, floorplanning, and Power-Performance-Area (PPA) target setting.
reference: Synopsys Design Compiler; Cadence Innovus; SEMI Standards

description: Estimated Non-Recurring Engineering (NRE) cost in US dollars associated with developing this RTL specification. Used for project budgeting, customer design-in pricing, and financial reporting in SAP S/4HANA CO module.

Date on which this RTL specification was marked obsolete, typically superseded by a newer version or upon product End of Life (EOL). Supports Product Change Notification (PCN) and Last Time Buy (LTB) processes.
Number of distinct power domains defined in the Unified Power Format (UPF) or Common Power Format (CPF) specification for this RTL block. Drives low-power verification and power intent analysis.
reference: IEEE Std 1801 (UPF); Cadence Innovus; Synopsys Design Compiler

description: Standard format used to specify power intent for this RTL design block. UPF (IEEE 1801) and CPF (Cadence) are the two industry standards. 'none' indicates no multi-voltage power management is implemented.
reference: IEEE Std 1801 (UPF); Cadence Innovus; Synopsys Design Compiler

description: Full path or URL to the revision control repository location where the RTL source files for this specification are stored (e.g., Git remote URL or Perforce depot path). Classified confidential as it reveals internal IP infrastructure.
Reset architecture employed in this RTL design block. Defines whether resets are synchronous, asynchronous, or mixed, which impacts timing closure, DFT scan insertion, and silicon reliability.
reference: IEEE Std 1800; Synopsys Design Compiler; JEDEC

description: Version control system in which the RTL source files for this specification are managed. Enables provenance tracking and audit trail for design changes.

Date on which this RTL specification was formally approved through the PLM design review process. Marks the effective start of the specification as a binding design baseline. Required for ISO 9001 and IATF 16949 design record compliance.

Externally-known, human-readable unique identifier for the RTL specification artifact as tracked in Siemens Teamcenter PLM and revision control systems (Git, Perforce). Used for cross-system traceability and design review references.
reference: Siemens Teamcenter PLM; Oracle Agile PLM

description: Date on which this RTL specification was released for downstream use (synthesis, physical design, verification). Distinct from approval date; release may follow approval after additional sign-off steps.
reference: Siemens Teamcenter PLM; Oracle Agile PLM; ISO 9001

description: Current lifecycle state of the RTL specification artifact within the PLM workflow. Controls downstream design activities: 'draft' allows edits; 'approved' gates synthesis; 'released' permits tapeout submission; 'obsolete' marks superseded versions.
reference: Siemens Teamcenter PLM; Oracle Agile PLM; ISO 9001
